questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Nature and Scope
questions.question: Which sub-field of Human Geography interfaces directly with the sister social science discipline of Psychology?
options: A) Behavioural Geography
B) Electoral Geography
C) Historical Geography
D) Military Geography
questions.explanation: Behavioural geography studies human spatial perception, cognitive mental maps, and decision-making, drawing heavily from psychology.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Nature and Scope
questions.question: The sub-field of 'Electoral Geography', which investigates voting trends, ballot patterns, and parliamentary constituency delineation, is an interface with:
options: A) Anthropology and Paleontology
B) Psephology and Political Science
C) Geomorphology and Hydrology
D) Agricultural Botany
questions.explanation: Electoral geography examines the spatial aspects of elections, voting behavior, and delimitation of electoral districts in close synergy with political science and psephology.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: People
questions.question: How is 'Physiological Population Density' distinguished mathematically from crude population density?
options: A) Total Agricultural Labourers divided by Gross Irrigated Land
B) Total Urban Population divided by Built-up Municipal Area
C) Total Population divided by Net Cultivated (Arable) Land
D) Total Rural Population divided by Total Forest Area
questions.explanation: Physiological density measures population pressure directly on agricultural resources, calculated as Total Population / Net Cultivated Area.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: People
questions.question: 'Agricultural Density' is an essential demographic indicator computed as the ratio of:
options: A) Total Urban Working Population to Net Sown Area
B) Total Livestock Herd Size to Permanent Pasture Acreage
C) Total Culturable Wasteland to Gross Irrigated Area
D) Total Agricultural Population to Net Cultivated (Arable) Land Area
questions.explanation: Agricultural density isolates the farming community (cultivators and agricultural laborers and their dependents) relative to net arable land.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: People
questions.question: Unlike India, where the sex ratio is calculated as the number of females per 1,000 males, in many Western countries it is defined as:
options: A) Number of males per 1,000 (or per 100) females
B) Number of female live births per gross square kilometer
C) Total adult females divided by total infant deaths
D) Total working women divided by total elderly men
questions.explanation: In European and North American demographic conventions, the sex ratio is expressed as the number of males per 100 or 1,000 females: (Male Population / Female Population) × 1000.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: People
questions.question: Under the UNDP Human Development Report scoring criteria, countries having an HDI score between 0.700 and 0.799 are classified into which group?
options: A) Very high human development
B) High human development
C) Medium human development
D) Low human development
questions.explanation: Countries scoring 0.800 and above fall in 'Very High', while those between 0.700 and 0.799 are grouped in the 'High' human development tier.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: People
questions.question: Which of the following dimensions is NOT included in calculating the Human Development Index (HDI)?
options: A) Life expectancy at birth (health)
B) Expected and mean years of schooling (education)
C) Total national defense military expenditure
D) Gross National Income (GNI) per capita in Purchasing Power Parity (decent standard of living)
questions.explanation: HDI measures average achievement across three fundamental dimensions: a long and healthy life, knowledge/education, and a decent standard of living.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Human Activities
questions.question: Why is underground (shaft) mining recognized as far more hazardous to human labour than open-cast surface quarrying?
options: A) It exposes workers directly to harsh tropical desert sunstrokes
B) It requires digging exclusively with bare hands without electricity
C) It operates only during night hours under severe winter blizzards
D) Mines are susceptible to poisonous gas explosions, underground fires, cave-ins, and flooding of deep shafts
questions.explanation: Underground shaft mining involves dangerous working conditions, including methane and carbon monoxide asphyxiation, roof collapses, underground flooding, and fires.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Human Activities
questions.question: Gathering as a primary economic pursuit is practiced in high-latitude zones encompassing which geographical territory?
options: A) Northern Canada, northern Eurasia, and southern Chile
B) The Mediterranean coastal basin of southern Europe
C) The fertile delta plains of the Yangtze and Ganga
D) The central corn belt of the Midwestern United States
questions.explanation: High-latitude gathering zones include northern Canada, northern Eurasia (Siberia), and southern Chile, where harsh cold limits agricultural cultivation.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Human Activities
questions.question: Which of the following is a classic plantation crop introduced into tropical Southeast Asia (particularly Malaysia) by European planters?
options: A) Barley
B) Natural rubber
C) Rye
D) Oats
questions.explanation: Rubber was brought from the Amazon basin and planted extensively in Malaysia and Indonesia by the British and Dutch as a major plantation crop.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Human Activities
questions.question: Which unique climatic feature of the Mediterranean agricultural region enables the commercial cultivation of premium citrus fruits and olives?
options: A) Perennial continuous snowfall throughout the year
B) High daily torrential equatorial afternoon rains
C) Mild, wet winters and warm, dry sunny summers
D) Dense summer fog and sub-zero winter permafrost
questions.explanation: Mediterranean climate is characterized by winter rainfall brought by westerlies and dry warm sunny summers, perfect for citrus crops, olives, and viticulture.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Human Activities
questions.question: The Tata Iron and Steel Company (TISCO) at Jamshedpur was established in 1907 at the confluence of which two rivers to ensure perennial water supply?
options: A) Damodar and Barakar
B) Mahanadi and Brahmani
C) Ganga and Son
D) Subarnarekha and Kharkai
questions.explanation: TISCO at Jamshedpur was strategically built near the confluence of the Subarnarekha and Kharkai rivers, close to haematite mines of Mayurbhanj and Jharia coking coal.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Human Activities
questions.question: Industrial enterprises that are jointly established and managed by the government and private sector companies are classified as:
options: A) Joint sector industries
B) Public sector undertakings
C) Sole proprietorships
D) Cooperative societies
questions.explanation: Joint sector industries are managed jointly by the state and private individuals or consortiums (e.g., Oil India Limited).

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Human Activities
questions.question: In developing countries like India, the cotton textile manufacturing sector is uniquely divided into which three operational segments?
options: A) Cottage guilds, robotic nanotechnology, and deep sea processing
B) Handloom sector, powerloom sector, and composite mill sector
C) State defense armories, export cooperatives, and aviation mills
D) Heavy foundry sector, cryogenic blast sector, and chemical synth sector
questions.explanation: Cotton textiles in India operate across: handloom (labor-intensive cottage weaving), powerloom (semi-mechanized decentralized units), and large integrated composite mills.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Human Activities
questions.question: The informal service sector in developing urban cities is characterized by:
options: A) High corporate executive salaries and multinational stock options
B) Extensive state pension guarantees and permanent medical coverage
C) Unorganized, low-wage personal services such as domestic maids, street vendors, and auto-rickshaw drivers
D) Automated algorithmic high-frequency trading terminals
questions.explanation: The informal or unorganized tertiary sector absorbs millions of unskilled rural migrants in precarious, unregulated, low-paid informal urban services.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Human Activities
questions.question: The 'Digital Divide' in human geography refers to the wide disparity in:
options: A) The mathematical distance between primary iron mines and coastal ports
B) The ratio of agricultural tractors to manual wooden ploughs
C) The geographical elevation gap between sea level and high mountain plateaus
D) Access to Information and Communication Technology (ICT) across different countries and between urban and rural populations
questions.explanation: The Digital Divide reflects spatial and socioeconomic inequalities in opportunities to access and utilize computers, the internet, and digital information systems.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Human Activities
questions.question: What is the primary factor that distinguishes Quaternary economic activities from conventional Tertiary services?
options: A) Quaternary activities involve intellectual capital, research, and generation/processing of complex knowledge and information
B) Quaternary activities deal exclusively with the physical extraction of iron ore and bauxite
C) Quaternary activities require no formal education or computer equipment
D) Quaternary activities involve only manual personal grooming like barbering
questions.explanation: While tertiary activities provide general services, quaternary activities represent specialized knowledge-based services, software engineering, and strategic R&D.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Transport, Communication and Trade
questions.question: The industrial Ruhr coal district in Germany is connected directly to the Rhine waterway through the inland river port of:
options: A) Hamburg
B) Duisburg
C) Frankfurt
D) Munich
questions.explanation: Duisburg, situated at the confluence of the Rhine and Ruhr rivers, is the world's largest inland river port, handling massive coal, iron, and chemical barge traffic.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Transport, Communication and Trade
questions.question: Which canal connects Lake Superior and Lake Huron, allowing large lake freighters to bypass the St. Mary's rapids?
options: A) The Welland Canal
B) The Erie Canal
C) The Soo Canal (Sault Ste. Marie)
D) The Corinth Canal
questions.explanation: The Soo Canal (Sault Ste. Marie) bypasses the rapids between Lake Superior and Lake Huron, enabling iron ore and grain freighters to navigate the Great Lakes.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Transport, Communication and Trade
questions.question: The South Atlantic Sea Route links Western Europe and West Africa across the Atlantic Ocean with which developing economic region?
options: A) Japan, South Korea, and China in East Asia
B) India, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka in South Asia
C) Australia and New Zealand in Oceania
D) Brazil, Argentina, and Uruguay in South America
questions.explanation: The South Atlantic Sea Route traverses the Atlantic, connecting ports in Western Europe and West Africa with Santos, Rio de Janeiro, Buenos Aires, and Montevideo.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Transport, Communication and Trade
questions.question: The COMECON pipeline was constructed by the former Soviet Union to transport crude petroleum across over 4,000 km from the Volga-Urals basin to:
options: A) Eastern European countries including Poland, East Germany, Hungary, and Czechoslovakia
B) South Asian ports on the Arabian Sea
C) Sub-Saharan African mining enclaves
D) Pacific coastal cities in western Canada
questions.explanation: The COMECON (Druzhba or 'Friendship') pipeline was built to supply Soviet crude oil to socialist allies in Eastern Europe.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Transport, Communication and Trade
questions.question: Ports that specialize in handling bulk industrial cargoes such as crude petroleum, iron ore, coal, and bulk grains are categorized as:
options: A) Packet passenger ports
B) Industrial ports
C) Naval fortress ports
D) River ferry terminals
questions.explanation: Industrial ports are equipped with mechanized bulk-handling gear, deep drafts, and pipelines specifically designed to load and discharge heavy raw materials.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - People
questions.question: In the Census of India, the economically active working population is divided into which four standard industrial categories?
options: A) White-collar executives, Blue-collar mechanics, Farmers, and Students
B) Primary miners, Secondary weavers, Tertiary traders, and Government officers
C) Cultivators, Agricultural Labourers, Household Industry Workers, and Other Workers
D) Landlords, Peasant tenants, Factory owners, and Retailers
questions.explanation: The Census of India classifies all workers into four broad categories: Cultivators, Agricultural Labourers, Household Industry Workers, and Other Workers.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - People
questions.question: What proportion of India's total workforce is engaged in the primary agricultural sector (as cultivators and agricultural labourers) according to Census 2011?
options: A) 28.4 percent
B) 72.8 percent
C) 41.2 percent
D) 54.6 percent
questions.explanation: According to Census 2011, about 54.6% of total workers in India are engaged in agricultural activities (31.8% agricultural laborers and 22.8% cultivators).

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - Human Settlements
questions.question: To be classified as a 'Census Town' in India, an urban settlement must satisfy which specific demographic criteria?
options: A) Minimum population of 5,000, at least 75% of male main workers in non-agricultural pursuits, and density of at least 400 persons per sq km
B) Minimum population of 50,000, 100% literate citizens, and an operational international civil airport
C) Notification as a statutory municipality by the state legislative assembly regardless of population
D) Presence of at least three operational public sector heavy manufacturing plants
questions.explanation: Census Towns are non-statutory urban settlements that meet three criteria: pop >= 5,000, >= 75% of male main workers in non-agricultural work, and density >= 400 persons/km².

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - Human Settlements
questions.question: Mhow (Dr. Ambedkar Nagar in Madhya Pradesh) and Kamptee (in Maharashtra) were established historically as:
options: A) Ancient religious temple centers
B) Military garrison and cantonment towns
C) Major marine pearl-fishing ports
D) Capital administrative metropolises
questions.explanation: Mhow and Kamptee were established by the British military administration to station military regiments and cantonment commands.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - Human Settlements
questions.question: Which of the following ports was developed as a 'Modern Town' by the British along the western coast of India?
options: A) Madurai
B) Pataliputra
C) Mumbai
D) Ujjain
questions.explanation: Modern towns in India were developed during British and European colonial expansion, establishing port footholds at Surat, Goa, Mumbai, Chennai, and Kolkata.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - Resources and Development
questions.question: Over the past six decades, which land-use category in India has shown the most consistent and substantial percentage increase?
options: A) Permanent pastures and grazing lands
B) Culturable wastelands
C) Barren and unculturable rocky lands
D) Area under non-agricultural uses
questions.explanation: Area under non-agricultural uses (buildings, roads, industrial infrastructure, urban housing) has risen steadily due to rapid urbanization and economic expansion.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - Resources and Development
questions.question: Although Uttar Pradesh produces the largest total volume of wheat in India, which state achieves the highest yield per hectare (over 4,000 kg/ha)?
options: A) Punjab
B) Bihar
C) Madhya Pradesh
D) Rajasthan
questions.explanation: Punjab achieves the highest per-hectare wheat yields in India due to near-100% canal and tube-well irrigation coverage, HYV seeds, and heavy fertilizer inputs.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - Resources and Development
questions.question: Which of the following is the single largest pulse crop produced in India, accounting for nearly 40% of total pulse production?
options: A) Tur (arhar)
B) Gram (chickpea)
C) Urad (black gram)
D) Moong (green gram)
questions.explanation: Gram is the leading pulse cultivated in India, grown predominantly in Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, and Maharashtra during the Rabi season.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - Resources and Development
questions.question: Why is commercial tea cultivation concentrated along well-drained undulating hill slopes in the Brahmaputra valley and Nilgiris rather than flat plains?
options: A) Tea leaves require sub-zero winter snowfall to develop caffeine content
B) Flat plains are legally reserved exclusively for atomic reactor testing
C) Tea bushes cannot tolerate stagnant water around their roots, demanding deep friable acidic loamy soils on gentle hill slopes
D) Hill breezes prevent tea leaves from turning green during photosynthesis
questions.explanation: While tea requires heavy rainfall (150–250 cm), water stagnation is fatal to tea root systems; hence, well-drained mountain slopes are required.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - Resources and Development
questions.question: In the hyper-arid Jaisalmer district of Rajasthan, traditional earthen embankments constructed across agricultural slopes to impound runoff and saturate fields for winter cropping are known as:
options: A) Baolis
B) Guhls
C) Zings
D) Khadins
questions.explanation: Khadins are indigenous water-harvesting systems designed by the Paliwal Brahmins of Jaisalmer, creating fertile moist soil beds for winter rabi crops.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - Resources and Development
questions.question: In the lower Ganga plains of West Bengal and Bihar, deep tube-well over-pumping has triggered serious public health concerns due to natural leaching of which toxic element?
options: A) Arsenic
B) Mercury
C) Uranium
D) Cadmium
questions.explanation: Excessive groundwater withdrawal in the Bengal alluvial basin exposes arsenic-rich pyrite sediments, leaching dangerous dissolved arsenic into village drinking wells.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - Resources and Development
questions.question: The Malanjkhand copper belt, India's largest single open-cast copper mining operation, is located in the Balaghat district of:
options: A) Rajasthan
B) Madhya Pradesh
C) Jharkhand
D) Karnataka
questions.explanation: Malanjkhand in the Balaghat district of Madhya Pradesh accounts for more than half of India's domestic copper ore production.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - Resources and Development
questions.question: The Nellore mica belt, famous for the extraction of green-tinted muscovite mica, is situated in which state?
options: A) Karnataka
B) Tamil Nadu
C) Andhra Pradesh
D) Odisha
questions.explanation: Andhra Pradesh's Nellore district is renowned for producing superior quality electrical-grade tinted mica.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - Resources and Development
questions.question: The Talcher coalfield, possessing massive reserves of thermal coal that fuel regional super thermal power stations, is situated in the valley of which river?
options: A) Damodar river in West Bengal
B) Godavari river in Telangana
C) Son river in Madhya Pradesh
D) Mahanadi river in Odisha
questions.explanation: Talcher coalfield in the Angul-Dhenkanal tract of Odisha is located in the Mahanadi river basin, supplying thermal coal across eastern India.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - Resources and Development
questions.question: In Rajasthan, large-scale commercial wind power projects have been successfully developed around which desert district with high wind speeds?
options: A) Jaisalmer
B) Jaipur
C) Alwar
D) Kota
questions.explanation: Jaisalmer's vast open desert plains experience steady high-velocity winds, making it one of India's foremost wind energy generation hubs.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - Resources and Development
questions.question: In the Command Area of the Indira Gandhi Canal, what is the 'Warabandi System' implemented by the irrigation department?
options: A) A legal prohibition on building brick houses within 50 km of canal distributaries
B) A strict rotational water-distribution schedule that allocates water turns to farmers based on holding size
C) A tax penalty imposed on farmers planting leguminous gram pulses
D) A military curfew preventing livestock from grazing near canal banks
questions.explanation: Warabandi is an equitable water distribution system that allocates predetermined weekly water turns to individual farmers in proportion to their landholding.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - Resources and Development
questions.question: The modern concept of Sustainable Development harmonizes economic growth with which two other fundamental imperatives?
options: A) Military territorial conquest and industrial mechanization
B) Complete national isolation and elimination of all foreign trade
C) Ecological preservation and social equity across generations
D) Massive urbanization and total deforestation of mountain watersheds
questions.explanation: Sustainable development integrates three interconnected pillars: economic viability, environmental protection, and social equity across current and future generations.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - Transport, Communication and International Trade
questions.question: National Highway 44 (NH-44), the backbone of the North-South Corridor and the longest national highway in India, connects:
options: A) Silchar in Assam to Porbandar in Gujarat
B) Delhi to Kolkata via Varanasi
C) Mumbai to Chennai via Pune and Bengaluru
D) Srinagar in Jammu & Kashmir to Kanyakumari in Tamil Nadu
questions.explanation: NH-44 spans 3,745 km from Srinagar in the extreme north to Kanyakumari at the southern tip of the Indian peninsula.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - Transport, Communication and International Trade
questions.question: The East-West Corridor of the National Highways Development Project (NHDP) connects:
options: A) Silchar in Assam to Porbandar in Gujarat
B) Kolkata in West Bengal to Mumbai in Maharashtra
C) Guwahati in Assam to Amritsar in Punjab
D) Bhubaneswar in Odisha to Surat in Gujarat
questions.explanation: The East-West highway corridor spans 3,300 km connecting Silchar in Assam with the port city of Porbandar on the Gujarat coast.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - Transport, Communication and International Trade
questions.question: Which major seaport on the east coast, situated 25 km north of Chennai, was established as India's first corporate port to handle thermal coal and cars?
options: A) Visakhapatnam Port
B) Ennore Port (Kamarajar Port)
C) Paradip Port
D) Tuticorin Port
questions.explanation: Kamarajar Port at Ennore was commissioned as a dedicated energy and corporate port to relieve severe bulk cargo pressure on Chennai Port.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - Transport, Communication and International Trade
questions.question: V.O. Chidambaranar Port (formerly Tuticorin Port) on the Tamil Nadu coast has a specialized artificial deep-water harbour designed to handle trade primarily with:
options: A) Greenland and Arctic research settlements
B) Chile and Peru across the Southern Pacific
C) Sri Lanka and neighboring Indian Ocean island nations
D) Western Canada and Alaska across the Bering Strait
questions.explanation: V.O. Chidambaranar Port in the Gulf of Mannar handles extensive cargo, thermal coal, fertilizers, and container transit to and from Sri Lanka.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues
questions.question: In India's National Air Quality Index (AQI), which fine particulate pollutant poses the greatest danger to pulmonary and cardiovascular health due to deep alveolar penetration?
options: A) Particulate Matter 100 (PM100)
B) Inert argon gas molecules
C) Suspended sea salt crystals
D) Particulate Matter 2.5 (PM2.5)
questions.explanation: PM2.5 particles are smaller than 2.5 micrometers; when inhaled, they penetrate deep into lung alveoli and enter the bloodstream, causing serious cardiovascular and respiratory disease.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues
questions.question: What parameter is utilized by the Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) as the primary chemical indicator of organic waste pollution and sewage contamination in Indian rivers?
options: A) Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) and Fecal Coliform counts
B) Total dissolved radioactive radon isotopes
C) Ambient atmospheric barometric pressure above the river
D) Water surface seismic wave reflectivity
questions.explanation: High Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD) indicates heavy depletion of dissolved oxygen caused by decomposing organic sewage, while fecal coliform bacteria indicate human waste contamination.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - Geographical Perspective on Selected Issues
questions.question: In the Aravalli range of Rajasthan and Haryana, rapid desertification and loss of groundwater recharge have been accelerated by:
options: A) Continuous volcanic eruptions coating mountain slopes in molten basalt
B) Unregulated open-cast stone quarrying and deforestation destroying the natural green buffer against the Thar desert
C) Constructing extensive subsurface railway tunnels beneath granite hills
D) Planting millions of indigenous neem trees across hill slopes
questions.explanation: Illegal quarrying for quartzite and marble in the Aravallis has stripped the hills of vegetation and breached the natural geological barrier protecting eastern Rajasthan and Delhi from desert sand expansion.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Nature and Scope
questions.question: In Griffith Taylor's concept of Neo-determinism, a human being's role in altering nature is compared to a:
options: A) Master who exerts absolute, unfettered tyranny over physical elements
B) Helpless captive slave bound entirely by nature's iron laws
C) Traffic controller who can change the speed of flow but cannot alter the fundamental direction of the road
D) Computer programmer designing digital virtual realities
questions.explanation: Taylor used the traffic controller analogy: humans can accelerate, slow, or halt the speed of development, but cannot defy nature's physical laws without causing catastrophic disasters.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Transport, Communication and Trade
questions.question: Why does the Panama Canal require an intricate system of six locks (such as the Miraflores and Gatun locks) to lift and lower ships across the Isthmus?
options: A) Because tidal currents in the Pacific are ten times faster than sound waves
B) Because the Pacific Ocean is legally required to remain at lower pressure than the Atlantic
C) Because locks are required to filter out dangerous sea monsters from the Caribbean Sea
D) Because ships must be lifted 26 metres above sea level to cross the artificial Gatun Lake and Continental Divide
questions.explanation: The Panama Canal uses locks to lift ships 26 meters to the level of Lake Gatun and then lower them back to sea level on the other side.

questions.topic: India: People and Economy - Transport, Communication and International Trade
questions.question: Which port on the western coast of India is a spacious natural harbour and historically the premier commercial gateway handling the country's foreign trade?
options: A) Kandla Port
B) Marmagao Port
C) Mumbai Port
D) Kochi Port
questions.explanation: Mumbai Port is a large natural deep-water harbour situated on the western coast of Maharashtra, serving a vast industrialized hinterland.

questions.topic: Fundamentals of Human Geography: Transport, Communication and Trade
questions.question: The Rhine waterway in Europe is navigable for ocean-going freighters from its mouth at Rotterdam up to which Swiss inland city over a stretch of 700 km?
options: A) Geneva
B) Zurich
C) Bern
D) Basel
questions.explanation: The Rhine is navigable for a length of 700 km from the port of Rotterdam on the North Sea all the way upstream to Basel in Switzerland.
